newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Interim sees gain, lower debt.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Interim sees gain, lower debt.

text.p: Interim Services Inc, a provider of commercial and professional temporary personnel and other human resource services, expects to record a small gain from the sale of its healthcare unit over its book value, netting proceeds of about $100 million.
"We think we will net proceeds of about $100 million," said Ray Marcy, chief executive officer in a telephone interview Monday. "I think there will be a small gain."

On Monday, Interim Services said that it has a definitive agreement to sell its Interim Healthcare business to Cornerstone Equity Investors for $134 million and that it plans to use the proceeds to pay down debt.
"This would bring our debt to capital (ratio) down to the mid forties," Marcy said. Debt is currently 52 to 55 percent of capital.
Marcy said he is comfortable with analysts' consensus earnings estimate of $0.48 a share for the second quarter and $2.12 a share for the year, exclusive of the divestiture.
"We will see some dilution with the divestment...If the transaction closes in the fourth quarter, we could have dilution more than 10 percent in that quarter," Marcy noted.
"The transaction will be substantially less dilutive in 1998 than in 1997, if at all," he said.
Marcy said he expects the sale to help boost the company's stock price, calling the healthcare component "volatile."
Interim Services stock was up 2-13/16 to 44-1/16 on the New York Stock Exchange.
